source_text: Mirarer psychicos istos, si sola luxuria tenerentur, qua saepius nubunt, si non etiam ingluuie lacerarentur, qua ieiunia oderunt. monstrum scilicet haberetur libido sine gula, cum duo haec tam unita atque concreta sint, ut si disiungi omnino potuissent, ipsi prius uentri pudenda non adhaererent. specta corpus, et una regio est. denique pro dispositione membrorum ordo uitiorum. prior uenter, et statim cetera saginae substructa lasciuia est; per edacitatem salacitas transit. agnosco igitur animalem fidem studio carnis, qua tota constat, tam multiuorantiae quam multinubentiae pronam, ut merito spiritalem disciplinam pro substantia aemulam in hac quoque specie continentiae accuset perinde gulae frenos imbuentem per nullas interdum uel seras uel aridas escas, quemadmodum et libidini per unicas nuptias. piget iam cum talibus congredi, pudet etiam de eis altercari quorum nec defensio uerecunda est. quomodo enim protegam castitatem et sobrietatem sine taxatione aduersariorum? quinam isti sint, semel nominabo: exteriores et interiores botuli psychicorum. hi paracleto controuersiam faciunt; propter hoc nouae prophetiae recusantur; non quod alium deum praedicent Montanus et Priscilla et Maximilla, nec quod Iesum Christum soluant, nec quod aliquam fidei aut spei regulam euertant, sed quod plane doceant saepius ieiunare quam nubere. de modo quidem nubendi iam edidimus monogamiae defensionem. nunc de castigatione uictus secunda uel magis prima continentiae pugna est. arguunt nos, quod ieiunia propria custodiamus, quod stationes plerumque in uesperam producamus, quod etiam xerophagias obseruemus siccantes cibum ab omni carne et omni iurulentia et uuidioribus quibusque pomis nec quid uinositatis uel edamus uel potemus; lauacri quoque abstinentiam, congruentem arido uictui. nouitatem igitur obiectant, de cuius inlicito praescribant aut haeresin iudicandam, si humana praesumptio est, aut pseudoprophetiam pronuntiandam, si spiritalis indictio est, dum quaque ex parte anathema audiamus, qui aliter adnuntiamus.
thought_title: The belly and the bed: why opponents hate fasting
orientation: Tertullian opens his treatise by attacking the unspiritual Christians who oppose the New Prophecy's fasting practices, tracing their hostility to gluttony and lust.
pass_a_gloss: I would be amazed at these unspiritual Christians, if they were held by luxury alone, by which they marry rather often, if they were not also torn apart by gluttony, by which they hate fasts. A monster, of course, would lust be considered without gluttony, since these two are so united and grown together, that if they could be separated at all, the private parts would not first cling to the belly itself. Look at the body, and it is one region. In short, according to the arrangement of the members, there is an order of vices. First the belly, and immediately the rest of wantonness is built upon overindulgence; through greediness lust passes. I recognize therefore an animal faith by the zeal for the flesh, by which it wholly consists, prone as much to much-eating as to much-marrying, so that deservedly it accuses the spiritual discipline, as a rival to its substance, in this kind of self-control too, as it were putting the bridle on gluttony through no sometimes late or dry foods, just as also on lust through single marriages. It is already annoying to engage with such people, it is shameful even to dispute about them whose defense is not even respectable. For how shall I protect chastity and sobriety without taxing the adversaries? Who these are, I will name once: the outer and inner sausages of the unspiritual Christians. These make controversy for the Advocate; for this reason the New Prophecy is rejected; not that Montanus and Priscilla and Maximilla preach another god, nor that they dissolve Jesus Christ, nor that they overturn any rule of faith or hope, but that they plainly teach to fast more often than to marry. About the manner of marrying indeed we have already published a defense of monogamy. Now about the chastening of food is the second or rather the first battle of self-control. They accuse us, because we keep fasts of our own, because we often extend station fasts into the evening, because we also observe dry-food fasts, drying the food from all meat and all juiciness and from all the moister fruits, and we neither eat nor drink anything of winey quality; also abstinence from the bath, suited to the dry diet. Novelty therefore they object, about the unlawfulness of which they prescribe either that it be judged heresy, if it is human presumption, or that it be pronounced false prophecy, if it is a spiritual injunction, while on every side we hear anathema, who announce otherwise.

pass_b_english: I would be surprised at these unspiritual Christians if they were held only by luxury, since they marry rather often, and not also ruled by gluttony, since they hate fasting. Lust without gluttony would surely be considered a monster, since these two are so united and fused together that if they could be separated at all, the private parts would not be the first to cling to the belly. Look at the body: it is one region. In fact, the order of vices follows the arrangement of the members. The belly comes first, and immediately the rest of lust is built upon overindulgence; through greediness, lust passes over. I recognize, then, an unspiritual faith by its devotion to the flesh, of which it entirely consists, as prone to much eating as to much marrying, so that it rightly accuses spiritual discipline as hostile to its substance in this kind of self-control as well, since that discipline puts reins on gluttony through food that is sometimes none, sometimes late, sometimes dry, just as it does on lust through single marriages.

It is now tiresome to engage with such people; it is even shameful to dispute about them, since their defense is not even respectable. How am I to protect chastity and sobriety without assessing my opponents? Who they are I will name once: the outer and inner gluttons among the unspiritual Christians. These people make controversy against the Advocate, the Holy Spirit; for this reason the New Prophecy is rejected—not because Montanus and Priscilla and Maximilla preach another God, nor because they dissolve Jesus Christ, nor because they overturn any rule of faith or hope, but because they plainly teach fasting more often than marrying. About the manner of marrying, I have already published a defense of monogamy. Now the battle over the discipline of food is the second, or rather the first, fight for self-control.

They accuse us because we keep our own fasts, because we often extend station fasts until evening, because we also observe dry-food fasts, keeping our food free of all meat and all juiciness and any of the more succulent fruits, and we neither eat nor drink anything with a winey quality; we also abstain from bathing, which suits dry-food fasts. So they object to novelty, and from its unlawfulness they prescribe that it must be judged heresy if it is human presumption, or pronounced false prophecy if it is a spiritual command, so that on every side we hear anathema, we who proclaim otherwise.
